title: Canary Metrics + Dashboard Requirements (Hosted Rollouts GA)
body:
Context
- This doc defines requirements for canary dashboards for Hosted percentage rollouts (GA). The dashboards are used by:
  (1) customers inside Console to compare baseline vs candidate, and
  (2) SRE/on-call to detect/mitigate regressions quickly during rollouts.
- We need a consistent “compare view” that remains interpretable under sticky routing and streaming semantics, and we need to keep metric cardinality under control.

Non-negotiables (GA)
1) Baseline vs candidate compare views that clearly answer: “Is the candidate worse, and by how much?”
2) Confidence hints (lightweight, no heavy stats UI) that help avoid false positives on low traffic.
3) Alerting hooks that integrate with SRE policies and rollout guardrails (latency/error/cost deltas).
4) Cardinality limits + safe defaults that won’t melt metrics infra when customers have many routes/models.

Definitions
- Rollout: a policy on a Hosted route that splits traffic across variants (baseline/candidate).
- Variant: baseline or candidate (GA assumes exactly two variants for canary rollouts).
- Route: Hosted API route (customer-configured endpoint).
- Effective routing: resolved policy after applying account/route/region layers (as applicable).

Primary user stories
Customer (Console)
- As an engineer, I can open a rollout and see traffic distribution + key regressions (p50/p95 latency, 5xx, timeouts, token cost) comparing baseline vs candidate.
- As an engineer, I can filter by time window and region and understand whether the candidate is trending worse.
- As an engineer, I can export/share a “rollout status snapshot” (link) to my team.

SRE/On-call
- As on-call, I can quickly determine whether a spike is isolated to the candidate variant and whether rollback/pause is warranted.
- As on-call, I can see policy changes (weight edits, pauses, rollbacks) overlaid on metrics.
- As on-call, I have alerts that page on meaningful deltas, not noise.

Executive/PM
- As PM, I can see aggregate adoption and incident reduction trends (not in GA dashboard scope, but note for future: product analytics view).

Dashboard inventory (what we are building)
A) Rollout Overview (per-rollout, customer-facing in Console)
- Header: route name/id, baseline model+version, candidate model+version, current split, rollout status (active/paused/rolled back/completed).
- Activity overlay: weight change events (policy version) shown as vertical markers.
- Time controls: last 15m / 1h / 6h / 24h / custom.
- Filters: region (optional), status code class, request type (chat/embeddings/etc if available), streaming vs non-streaming (if available).

B) Canary Compare (baseline vs candidate) (per-rollout)
Required panels (each with baseline, candidate, and delta):
1. Traffic
   - Requests/sec by variant
   - % traffic by variant (observed, not just configured)
   - Note: if stickiness enabled, show “distinct sticky keys” (or proxy) if available; otherwise annotate “sticky routing enabled” in UI.
2. Errors
   - 5xx rate by variant
   - 429 rate by variant (rate limiting / quota)
   - Timeout rate by variant (client timeout and server timeout if separated)
   - Top error reasons (bucketed) by variant (bounded set; see cardinality section)
3. Latency
   - p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency by variant
   - Time to first token (TTFT) for streaming routes (if streaming)
   - Token throughput (tokens/sec) by variant (optional but useful for “feels slower” debugging)
4. Cost / Token usage (Hosted)
   - Input tokens / output tokens per request by variant (avg + p95 if feasible)
   - Estimated $ / 1K tokens or $ / request by variant (Nadia to confirm canonical metric)
   - Cache hit rate (prefix/KV) by variant (if exposed at route level; otherwise omit)

C) SRE Canary Triage (internal; can be a Grafana template)
- Same panels as Canary Compare, but:
  - includes multiple rollouts view (table of active rollouts + deltas)
  - includes region breakdown to detect “one region stale weights”/propagation issues
  - includes control-plane propagation health signals (policy staleness, evaluation errors)

D) Alert Panels + Runbook Links
- A dedicated section that lists the canary-related alerts currently firing and links to:
  - hosted rollout pause/rollback runbook
  - rollout propagation SLO page

Compare view UX requirements
- Side-by-side + delta is required. Example rows:
  - p95 latency: baseline 420ms, candidate 510ms, +21%
  - 5xx rate: baseline 0.12%, candidate 0.35%, +0.23pp
- Delta formatting:
  - show both relative (%) and absolute (pp/ms/$) deltas where appropriate
  - use consistent color thresholds but keep minimal (we can’t rely solely on colors)
- “Observed vs configured split” callout:
  - if configured is 10% candidate but observed is 3–5%, add a warning: “Observed split differs from configured; check stickiness, sampling, or propagation.”
- Annotation events:
  - policy version changes, pause, rollback, schedule step transitions (if timed progression)
  - annotate with actor (if available) for internal dashboards; customer-facing can show “policy updated” without actor if needed.

Confidence hints (statistical, lightweight)
We need to communicate uncertainty without implementing a full stats product.

Requirements
- Each delta panel should include a small “confidence indicator” derived from sample size, not a hard gate.
- Show a short message when data is thin:
  - “Low traffic: interpret with caution (<N requests on candidate)”
  - “Candidate has <X% of baseline traffic in this window; widen window to increase confidence”

Proposed heuristic (v1)
- For rate metrics (5xx, timeouts): compute a Wilson interval or a simple normal approximation only if counts exceed minimum (e.g., candidate >= 200 requests). Otherwise display “insufficient data.”
- For latency metrics: require minimum sample size (e.g., candidate >= 200 requests) before showing a “High/Medium/Low confidence” badge. (Latency distributions are non-normal; we’re not promising p-values.)
- For cost metrics: same sample size gating.

Explicit non-goal
- We are not shipping formal hypothesis testing or sequential testing UI in GA. The goal is to prevent obvious misreads, not to certify regressions.

Alerting hooks (guardrails + SRE)
We need two layers:
1) Rollout guardrails (product feature): thresholds configured per rollout (latency/error/cost deltas) that can auto-pause/notify.
2) SRE alerts (platform): global alerts for systemic issues + propagation issues.

Alerting requirements
- Every alert must include tags sufficient to route triage:
  - route_id (or route_name), rollout_id, variant (when applicable), region (bounded), and metric type.
- Alerts should support “delta vs baseline” when comparing candidate performance.
- Alerts must link to:
  - the rollout in Console (customer-friendly deep link)
  - SRE dashboard view (internal)
  - pause/rollback runbook

Recommended initial alert set
A) Candidate regression alerts (per-rollout; only when rollout is active)
- Error rate delta: candidate 5xx_rate - baseline 5xx_rate > threshold for Y minutes
- Latency delta: candidate p95_latency - baseline p95_latency > threshold for Y minutes
- Cost delta: candidate $/request - baseline $/request > threshold for Y minutes

B) Rollout system health (global)
- Policy propagation staleness above SLO threshold (region-specific)
- Policy evaluation errors (control plane) above threshold
- Observed split mismatch (config vs observed) above tolerance for >Z minutes (this might be warning-only initially)

Cardinality + data model requirements
We need a minimal, stable set of dimensions that can power:
- baseline vs candidate comparisons
- per-route / per-rollout drill downs
- region breakdown for propagation issues

Required dimensions (must exist somewhere in pipeline)
- account_id (internal only; customer dashboards should scope by account implicitly)
- route_id (required)
- rollout_id (required for per-rollout dashboards; also needed to disambiguate multiple rollouts per route over time)
- variant (baseline|candidate)
- region (required, but limited to Redwood hosted regions)
- model_id + model_version (strongly preferred; otherwise at least “model_reference” string)

Strongly discouraged dimensions (cardinality risk)
- raw error strings, stack traces, prompt hashes, request ids
- customer-provided metadata keys
- fine-grained user/session ids

Error reason taxonomy (bounded)
- Define a small set of error_reason buckets (example):
  - upstream_timeout
  - overload
  - model_load_failed
  - invalid_request
  - auth_error
  - quota_rate_limited
  - internal_error
  - dependency_error
This enables “Top error reasons” without exploding labels.

Streaming considerations
- Metrics must not mix variants within a single streaming session.
- Variant selection should be pinned at request start and used for all stream chunks; metrics should be emitted with that pinned variant.
- For retries: attribute the retried request to the original pinned variant (or record a retry_outcome metric). This impacts how we interpret candidate error rates.

Open questions / decisions needed
1) What is the canonical join key between rollout policy and metrics?
   - Option A: rollout_id (generated at creation; stable)
   - Option B: route_id + policy_version
   - Risk: customers edit baseline/candidate model refs; how do we keep historical comparisons coherent?

2) How do we represent “candidate” when the candidate model version changes mid-rollout?
   - If candidate changes, do we treat it as a new rollout_id? Or keep rollout_id and store candidate_model_version as a dimension?
   - Recommendation: keep rollout_id but annotate “candidate changed” events and ensure model_version is available for filtering.

3) Observed split metric source of truth
   - Are we computing observed split from request counters in the data plane? If sampled, how accurate is it?
   - Need an explicit “sampling_rate” or documented sampling behavior for the compare view.

4) Region selection and aggregation
   - For customer-facing: default to “all regions” but allow drill-down.
   - For SRE: show region table by default.
   - Question: do we need per-AZ? Likely no for GA.

5) Quality gates integration
   - If quality gates exist (offline evals / prompt set regression), do we show them as:
     (a) a panel in the rollout dashboard, or
     (b) a separate “Quality” tab?
   - For GA: recommend simple status pill + link out to the eval report.

6) Cost metric definition
   - What is the GA-supported metric for “token cost delta”? Is it “metered_cost_usd” at request granularity?
   - Need Nadia confirmation + documentation alignment with billing.

7) How do we handle multi-step schedules (timed progression) in dashboard annotations?
   - We need a machine-readable event for “step advanced” to draw clean annotation markers.

8) How do we handle “rollout paused” semantics in charts?
   - Does paused mean candidate weight = 0 immediately? There may be propagation delay.
   - We should display configured weight and observed weight concurrently to show convergence.

Acceptance criteria (GA)
- For any active rollout, within Console we can show:
  - observed traffic split by variant
  - baseline vs candidate p95 latency and 5xx rate, with deltas
  - at least one cost/tokens panel with deltas
  - annotations for policy changes (weight edits/pause/rollback)
- For SRE, an internal dashboard exists that:
  - can list all active rollouts and sort by worst delta
  - provides region-level breakdown for at least errors/latency and staleness
- Cardinality guardrails are documented and enforced (or validated via load test) for per-variant tags.

Notes / next steps
- Logan/Thomas: finalize dimension set + error_reason taxonomy and confirm it matches Confluence standards.
- Allison/Aisha: confirm initial alert thresholds + paging policy (candidate regressions should generally be non-paging unless very severe; propagation issues may page).
- Paula: ensure we have consistent event emission for policy changes (create/update/pause/rollback) so dashboard annotations are reliable.
- Mina/Ravi: confirm how stickiness affects observed split + whether we can expose a “sticky_key_count” proxy.

Appendix: rough panel list (for dashboard JSON implementation)
- RPS (requests/sec) by variant
- Observed split % by variant
- p50/p95/p99 latency by variant
- TTFT p50/p95 (streaming)
- 5xx rate, 429 rate, timeout rate by variant
- Token in/out per request
- Estimated cost per request
- Propagation staleness by region
- Policy evaluation errors
- Table: active rollouts with key deltas + last policy change timestamp
